text:
On the morning the findings came out, the water at Ostrava Lake lay flat and grey, as it has through most of the winters anyone can remember. Beneath it, in layers thinner than a fingernail, sat a record of more than a century and a half.

That record was the subject of a study released on 12 March 2025 by Brennick University. Dr. Halvard Teskey, lead sedimentologist in the university's Department of Earth Systems, directed the work. His team analyzed 42 sediment cores, the longest reaching 6.8 meters in depth.

Lakes have long served as quiet archivists, each year adding a band of silt, organic matter and whatever the surrounding land sheds into the water. Reading those bands is slow work, and patience defines the field.

The report rests on the peer-reviewed paper "Layered Deposition Records in Ostrava Lake, 1850–2020," published in the *Journal of Limnological Studies*.
